newsitem.title: INDIA: Approval for Indian copper plant expansion soon.
newsitem.headline: Approval for Indian copper plant expansion soon.

text.p: Final approval by the Indian government for the expansion of the copper complex of the state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) will be taken up as a priority, the Mines Ministry said on Wednesday.
A ministry statement quoted Mines Minister Birendra Prasad Baishya as saying that HCL was undertaking expansion to become competitive and guard against wild fluctuations in world prices.

HCL proposes to expand its Khetri smelter and refining capacity, in the northern state of Rajasthan, to 100,000 tonnes per annum of copper from the present 31,000 tonnes at a cost of nearly 5.3 billion rupees.
The expansion would be partly based on imported concentrates with copper content of around 25-30 percent.
The expansion of the Khetri smelter would result in low operating costs and the use of workers with technical expertise, Baishya told a meeting of parliament deputies.
The statement said the project was expected to be commissioned within 22 months after government clearance.
India's estimated annual copper demand in the next few years is expected to be around 487,000 tonnes, up from a current 335,000.
Companies such as Sterlite Industries, Indo-Gulf Fertilisers and METDIST Ltd are in the process of setting up copper smelters in the country.
This would increase installed capacity to 316,000 tonnes per annum by 1999-2000.
